text: Hong Kong, Wednesday, Oct. 13, 1926.

label: text
text: BACK TO THE PARISH'PUMP!

label: text
text: With the passing of the boycott the parish pump will have a chance to come back into its own. Purely local affairs have been more or less under a cloud for sixteen months. The Colony has been content to "carry on" with the least possible attention to the local problems that matter—and many that do not!

label: text
text: The easiest thing in the day's life here is to find a complaint or a grievance. The Colony is simply swarming with them. But all eyes have been centred so much on Canton that may "handy annuals" have almost withered. Many, indeed, are sadly faded for lack of the necessary attention. It is a moot point whether this is all for the good. Goodness knows the community is not so articulate as it should be in years in which wars and strikes and boycotts play no part. Spasmodic efforts are made to create and sustain public interest in vital local problems; but the talk and the action are generally confined—like everything else here—to a select few who do not seem to mind shouldering other people's troubles and airing other people's grievances. The bulk of the community—and we write now only of the non-Chinese portion—are content to drift along in a happy-go-lucky fashion, hearing not and heeding not the turning of the parish pump handle. The call to real citizenship, sad to confess, apparently is heard by few.

label: text
text: Outside the Unofficial members of the Legislative Council and the Sanitary Board there is surely work for citizens of the Colony and citizens of the Empire—to make their influence felt; to stir up the dry bones in a too apathetic community; to arouse in them a sense of duty and of responsibility as residents of a British Colony and of the great Empire to whom they owe allegiance. That work need not necessarily be confined to grumbling and grousing and airing petty grievances. There is ample room in

label: text
text: ist as well as the destructionist. Why leave the entire settling of local destinies to the limited band of public men whose names figure in every scheme for the better

label: text
text: ment of the place in which we live?

label: text
text: If the passing of the boycott means a new innings for the parish pump, let our communal work be shared by many more than in the past. Good as is a Municipal Council for fostering the civic spirit the absence of such is no excuse for shunning and evading the duties of citizenship. A broader vision is required to cope successfully with local affairs. Mere denunciation of the parish pump because of its very parochialism will not lead to a solution of Hong Kong's problems. Parochialism, admittedly, can be carried to extremes, but there is always a happy mean that can easily be found by the individual desirous of leaving the Colony a better place than he found it.

label: paragraph_title
text: AUGMENT REPULSE BAY SERVICE

label: text
text: Two new and luxurious motor buses which have been added by the Hong Kong Hotel Garage to the Repulse Bay service will eliminate difficulty experienced in the past in maintaining a full service on all routes when any of the vehicles have been undergoing repairs.

label: text
text: The new cars are Miller built models on Studebaker chassis, the design and fittings making them the last word in comfortable travelling. Each passenger has a bucket seat, the cushions and backs being built on Barber double deck springs, amply padded and upholstered in brown leather, this together with the wide aisle and spacious windows making them ideal for local conditions.

label: text
text: Driven by Traffic Sergeant Mason and carrying seven passengers, one of the vehicles made a trial run to the town and back to the Central Police Station compound along Garden Road and Arbuthnot Road this morning

label: text
text:
The sharp gradients on the route gave ample scope for testing the efficiency of the brakes which acted smoothly even no sudden application without causing the passengers any discomfort.
With its blue painted body and large luggage box at the rear, the bus attracted considerable attention in the course of the trial run.

label: text
text: Including the driver who sits by himself, the bus has basket seats for 14 persons.

label: paragraph_title
text: ITALIAN OPERA

label: text
text: TO PLAY IN THE "STAR," KOWLOON.

label: text
text: Owing to a delay in the departure of the steamer conveying Carpi's Italian Opera Company to Manila, the company will open at the Star Theatre, Kowloon for three nights only commencing on Sunday afternoon, October 17

label: text
text: There will be a matinee on Sunday afternoon when “Barbiere of Siviglia will be staged and in the evening by special request, “Madame Butterfly” will be produced.

label: text
text: On Monday "Lucia de Lammermoor" will be played and on Tuesday the farewell performance will be "Aida."

label: text
text: The performances for the three last nights at the Theatre Royal are "Boheme" Rigoletto and "Carmen".

label: paragraph_title
text: CONVOY SYSTEM

label: text
text: PICKETS' DEPARTURE SEQUEL.

label: text
text: Among other matters dealt with at yesterday's meeting of the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce was that of the armed convoy system for the protection of shipping by the Hong Kong Government.

label: text
text: Some time ago, the opinion of the Chamber as to the desirability of reinstituting the convoy service was asked for by the then Colonial Secretary, but as the picket nuisance which was then in being hampered the movement of vessels on any large scale, the Chamber had not hitherto replied:

label: text
text: At yesterday's meeting, however, it was announced that, after consultation with the "principal shipping interests," the Chamber was in favour of advising the restoration of the convoy system.

label: text
text: Mr. Li Yau-tsun presided over the meeting supported by Mr. J. M. Wong, vice-chairman, and Mr. Ip. Lan-chuen, general secretary.

label: text
text: The question of "the better supervision of the searching of luggage and other packages by the police on outgoing and incoming steamers again came up for discussion. The problem before the Chamber was how to advise the Police Authorities on this matter, as it could not recommend the abolition of the practice, and it was considered impractical to ask for higher officials to direct the search in all cases.

label: text
text: After some “discussion, the matter was referred back to the Hotel Guild, which made the complaint with the suggestion that possibly a joint private meeting of representatives of the Guild and the Chamber might be held.

label: text
text: The secretary read a number of communications addressed to the Chamber, including one from the family of the late Mr. Ho Fook, thanking the Chamber for its sympathy in the family's recent bereavement, and one from the Chinese Society in Cuba advising against further Chinese emigration to that country.

label: paragraph_title
text: EVADING FARE.

label: paragraph_title
text: TWO EMPLOYEES USING ONE TICKET.

label: text
text: TRAMWAY CASE.

label: text
text: Mr. A. Gillard, of the Hong Kong Tramway Company, prosecuted two Chinese youths before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning with misuse of a monthly ticket.

label: text
text: Defendants were both employees of the Kin Yuen firm, of No. 26, Des Voeux Road. It was stated that the first defendant was found using the ticket on Tuesday, and when questioned gave the name appearing on the ticket and the address of the shop. The following day the second defendant used the ticket while travelling in a car.

label: text
text: Some difficulty arose when the second defendant said that his name was 'not Wong Kin-yuen, the name appearing on the ticket. Mr. Gillard said that the defendant was pointed out by a shop employee as the man bearing that name.

label: text
text: The first defendant, who admitted that he used a ticket not in his name, was fined $10. The case against the other youth was adjourned for one week for the master of the shop to be called.

label: paragraph_title
text: TYPHOON TOLL.

label: paragraph_title
text: JUNK WRECKED AT PO TOI ISLAND.

label: text
text: ELEVEN CASUALTIES.

label: text
text: Further details have been received regarding the rescue of thirty-three Chinese who were ast ashore on Po Toi island during the typhoon.

label: text
text:
These were the survivors of a trading junk which left Hoifung on Thursday carrying 39 passengers in addition to a crew of five.
The typhoon struck the vessel on the following day and broke it up on the rocks near the island.
On the receipt of the report at Stanley Police Station by the master of the grocery shop who attended to the needs of the survivors a launch proceeded to the island and brought them to Hong Kong yesterday.

label: text
text: Eleven persons perished in the disaster.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANTICS OF CHERVONETZ.

label: text
text:
Tokyo, October 7.—The Bank of Korea has suddenly announced the suspension of draft business at Vladivostok until, further notice, cwing to great fluctuations in the quotation of the chervonetz in Siberia, in spite of its stability in the European market.
It is noteworthy that the Bank of Korea is the only foreign Bank which the Soviet has permitted to open a branch in Soviet territory.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE RIGHT HORSE.

label: text
text: CANTON WILL CONQUER ALL CHINA.

label: text
text: KARAKHAN'S "TIP;"

label: paragraph_title
text: Vladivostok Oct. 6.

label: text
text: Ambassador Karakhan, the Russian envoy to Peking and probably the next Foreign Minister of the Soviet government, said in a news paper interview published to-day

label: text
text: that the Cantonese Army would be victorious in the present civil war and conquer the whole of China.

label: text
text: He arrived here yesterday from Shanghai and is on his way to Moscow via the Trans-Siberian railroad.

label: text
text: He predicted that the "people's army" of the north was rapidly reorganising itself and was anxious to free northern China "from the grip" of the reactionary forces under Marshal Chang Tso-lim. He said that the southern armies were actuated by a determination to suppress the unequal treaties between China and foreign powers.

label: text
text:
Moscow, Oct. 12.
M. Karakhan has arrived here
to consult the Soviet Government
on the Chinese situation.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLEGED PICKETS.

label: paragraph_title
text: A MAN WHO WAS A PROPER SOLDIER.

label: text
text: Two Chinese were charged at the Central Magistracy yesterday with the theft of a cargo of vegetables, valued at $426, from San Hui, Po On district, Chinese territory.

label: text
text:
Defendants were arrested when they brought the cargo to Hong Kong, and it was alleged by the prosecution that they were in the company of strike pickets who fired on the boat and took possession.
Mr. D. McCallum, who appeared for the defence, suggested that the complainants lost their own cargo of vegetables and accused the defendants who had brought their cargo down to Hong Kong of having stolen it.

label: text
text: One of the complainants who gave evidence at the first hearing of the case last week was cross-examined at length by Mr. McCallum and gave "interesting details of village life.

label: text
text:
Asked what occupation the first defendant followed, witness said he was formerly a farmer but now kept company with the pickets.
Mr. McCallum: You are a man of extraordinary little consequence in your village, aren't you?—I am a farmer in a small way.

label: text
text: During the whole of the time the strike and boycott has been operation has your village suffere at all?—No.

label: text
text: Have there ever been any pickets in your village at all?—I can't say. They might have been there while I was working in the fields. And throughout the strike you have been sending your produce to Hong Kong because it offers the best market open to you?—Yes.

label: text
text:
It has been your habit to sell produce to farmers who have formed themselves into a group, to bring it down to Hong Kong?—Yes.
Who is Commander Wong Lok?—He is in the country now.
Is there a magistrate called Luk Kwok-hang?—Yes...
And are you a soldier under Wong Lok?—I am not a soldier now. I gave it up during the fifth moon this year and returned to the village to do farming again.
You have made nothing but a nuisance of yourself ever since?—You can investigate. I was a

label: text
text:
Why did you give up your soldiering?—Because I couldn't make a living for my family.
Not even by looting? (Witness did not reply).
Have you been going round the village and demanding money?—No.

label: text
text:
Another complainant under cross-examination denied that he had had trouble with the defendants over ancestral funds and the suggestion that he lost his cargo and claimed that of the defendants as his own.
The case was adjourned.

label: paragraph_title
text: BANK CLOSURE.

label: paragraph_title
text: WINDING UP PETITION ADJOURNED

label: paragraph_title
text: RUSSO-ASIATIC BANK

label: text
text: In the Summary Court this morning (acting during the vacation for the Chief Justice in Bankruptcy), Mr. Justice Wood granted an adjournment in respect of an application for the winding up locally of the Russo-Asitic Bank.

label: text
text: Mr. H. G. Sheldon made the application, being instructed by Messrs. Johnson, Stokes and Master. He represented the petitioning creditor, Mr. Au Fung-chau.

label: text
text: The petition had been presented on September 28, Mr. Sheldon said, and the hearing fixed for to-day. The adjournment was asked for owing to certain documents not being yet available.

label: text
text: The Official Receiver, Mr. D. W. Tratman, had no objection and His Honour granted the adjournment, the necessary advertisement to be in the same form.

label: text
text: At Mr. Sheldon's "request," His Honour made a note that at this the first hearing the petition had "not been opposed.

label: text
text: [Another report on this subject appears on page 2, in the commercial section.]

label: paragraph_title
text: DRIVER IN TROUBLE.

label: text
text:
REMAND ON MANSLAUGHTER
CHARGE.

label: text
text: TRAFFIC PROSECUTIONS:

label: text
text: Manelaughter was the charge preferred against the driver of a motor lorry in the Kowloon Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: Defendant "was employed by the Sanitary Department. An old Chinese woman was knocked down at

label: text
text: the junction of Nathan Road and Saigon Street some days ago and she died subsequently.

label: text
text: Sub Inspector A. Nicoll of the Traffic Office, applied for a remand which was granted till next Tuesday.

label: text
text: His Worship (Mr. J. H. B. Nihil) fixed bail in the sum of $500 ($200 in cash and the balance by two sureties).

label: text
text: A fine of $25 was imposed by His Worship on the driver of another lorry for having an improper hand brake.

label: text
text: A Chinese "boy of 'about two years' was toddling across Canton Road when he was nearly run over by the lorry and this led to the prosecution.

label: text
text: Traffic Sergeant Smith prosecuted.

label: paragraph_title
text: "FLYING SQUAD."

label: paragraph_title
text: MEETING OF PROSPECTIVE MEMBERS.

label: text
text: Members of the Automobile Association having been circulated as to the willingness of any possessing motor cycles to join

label: text
text: the “flying squad” or volunteer corps attached to the police to assist in patrol and other work, a meeting of those signifying their willingness to join has been fixed for this evening when the duties of the proposed new corps will be explained.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER.

label: text
text: The official forecast of the weather, for Hong Kong and coast; till noon to-morrow is:—fresh, East winds fine.

label: text
text: Formosa Channel: Strong N.E. winds.

label: text
text: At 10.55 a.m. the Observatory reported:—

label: text
text: Pressure has decreased moderately at Nemuro and slightly at Aparri and Cape St. James. It is nearly stationary over Indo-China and has increased slightly elsewhere.

label: text
text: The anticyclone over China has rengthened slightly.

label: text
text: The typhoon is about 260 miles N.E. of Manila travelling West. It will probably continue "on this course towards Tourane.

label: text
text: Meteorological observations at 6 a.m. to day:—barometer 29.85; temperature 73; humidity 76; wind E.N.E., force 4; weather overcast.

label: text
text: Stout Wife (with fist aloft, to henpecked husband): You little, undersized, miserable worm! No wonder I met you at a garden fete!

label: text
text: Seeing a little girl crying bitterly in the street, a benevolent old man who was passing approach proached her and inquired what was the matter.

label: text
text: "I've lost a penny, sir," sobbed he child.

label: text
text: The old gentleman promptly thrust his hand into his pocket and brought forth a penny, which he gave her.

label: text
text: The little girl tried her eyes and look at him in surprise. "Oh, you wicked man!" she said. "So you had it all the time!"
